newsitem.title: USA: Oil union chief gets Tosco contract offer.
newsitem.headline: Oil union chief gets Tosco contract offer.

text.p: Members of the Oil, Chemical and Atomic Workers Union (OCAW) in California sent a final contract offer from refiner Tosco Corp to their chief for approval, a OCAW official said Wednesday.

Tosco, a refiner based in Stamford, Connecticut, has been negotiating with a team of 17 union officials a new contract for employees at four California refineries it will take over from Unocal Corp at the end of the month.
A union negotiator said he doubted OCAW president Robert Wages would approve the medical or pension plans Tosco is offering in the contract.
"We feel it's not quite what we were willing to settle for," said OCAW International representative Steve Sullivan.
He did not know how long it would take for Wages to examine the contract. Wages received the contract late Tuesday.
Union officials have said Tosco plans to cut up to 150 refinery jobs, and Sullivan said support runs strong for a strike if Tosco's offer fails to satisfy union members.
A Tosco executive declined to comment on the contract or possible strike.
